- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py, lines 145-146, `_GL0BAL_VALUE_OPTIONS` dict, `"gh": frozenset({"-R", "--repo"})` | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `gh` global-option list omits `--hostname`, a documented `gh` CLI option that takes a separate value. When a command uses it (`gh --hostname ghe.example.com api repos/x/y`), `_drop_global_value_options` does not skip the `--hostname` value, so `_segment_shape` treats `ghe.example.com` as the first positional and drops the subcommand `api`. `_family_word` then returns `gh` instead of `gh api`, merging distinct subcommand families.
  WHY: Permission-prompt shapes for `gh` operations using `--hostname` (GitHub Enterprise Server) are routed to the same family issue, grouping `gh api` and `gh issue view` under one `gh` family contrary to AD-1. This only affects GHE sessions, which are rare in this repositor's workflow.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py, lines 166-169, `_ISSUE_EXAMPLE_RE` regex; line 535-545, `legacy_issue_family` | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `legacy_issue_family` searches for `**Latest example**` unanchored anywhere in the issue body via `_ISSUE_EXAMPLE_RE`. The untrusted `**Reason Claude Code gave:**` section appears before the real example block. If a crafted reason text contains `**Latest example**` followed by a fenced command, `re.search` (with `re.S`, dotall) matches that first occurrence. With greedy `.*` between fences, the captured group includes the real example block as well, corrupting the parse and causing `legacy_issue_family` to return `None` (missing the correct legacy family) rather than injecting a specific wrong family.
  WHY: A legacy issue whose recorded example is parseable gets no family derived from it, so a later pattern of its family opens a new issue instead of commenting on the existing one.

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py, line 161 (`_ISSUE_EXAMPLE_RE`), lines 535-545 (`legacy_issue_family`) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The greedy `_ISSUE_EXAMPLE_RE` pattern with `re.S` can span multiple `**Latest example**` blocks when untrusted reason text contains that heading followed by a fenced command. The captured group then includes content from both the injected and real examples, producing a garbled command for `command_family` to parse.
  WHY: On a legacy issue (no family marker), `legacy_issue_family` derives the family from the captured example. A garbled multi-line capture either fails to parse (returning None, which falls through safely) or produces an unpredictable family key that could misroute later prompts. The attack requires crafting a reason string with `**Latest example**` and a matching fence length, which is narrow but not impossible given the 300-character-per-entry reason budget.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py, lines 145-147 (`_GLOBAL_VALUE_OPTIONS` for `gh`) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `gh` global-option set omits `--hostname`, which `gh` uses for GitHub Enterprise instances. For `gh --hostname ghe.example.com api ...`, `_drop_global_value_options` does not skip the hostname value, so `_segment_shape` treats it as positional 1 and the subcommand detection fails.
  WHY: `gh --hostname ghe.example.com api ...` and `gh --hostname ghe.example.com issue view ...` both get family word `gh` instead of `gh api` and `gh issue`, merging distinct subcommand prompts under one family. The fix is to add `"--hostname"` to the `gh` frozenset.

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py, line 169, `_ISSUE_EXAMPLE_RE`; line 535-545, `legacy_issue_family` | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `_ISSUE_EXAMPLE_RE` regex (`\*\*Latest example\*\*[^\n]*\n\n(`{4,})text\n(.*)\n\1`, with `re.S`) is unanchored. `legacy_issue_family` calls `re.search` on the entire issue body, which includes the untrusted "Reason Claude Code gave" section rendered before the real example block (lines 640-646). A reason string containing newlines could inject a `**Latest example**` heading followed by a blank line and a fenced block, causing `re.search` to match the injected heading instead of the real one. The greedy `(.*)` with `re.S` then captures from the injected fence to the last closing fence in the body, and `command_family` is called on that blob, potentially deriving the wrong family id.
  WHY: `legacy_issue_family` is called from `index_issues` (line 765) for every legacy `ai:permission-prompt` issue that has a signature marker but no generated family marker. A legacy issue whose reason text contains a crafted "Latest example" heading with a fence would be registered under the wrong family in `by_family`, causing `file_patterns` to post later reports as comments on the wrong family's issue.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py, line 146, `_GLOBAL_VALUE_OPTIONS["gh"]`; lines 454-467, `_drop_global_value_options` | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `gh` entry in `_GLOBAL_VALUE_OPTIONS` lists only `{-R, --repo}` but omits `--hostname`, a real `gh` CLI global flag that takes the next word as its value. For a command like `gh --hostname ghe.example.com api repos/...`, `_drop_global_value_options` does not skip `--hostname` or its value `ghe.example.com` (not in the known set), so the value is passed through as the first positional in `_segment_shape`. The subcommand `api` arrives at positional 2, where `_segment_shape` (line 243) only retains subcommands at `positionals == 1`. `_family_word` then iterates `shape[1:]` and finds only `--hostname` (starts with `-`, skipped) and `*` (the hostname value), so it returns just `gh` instead of `gh api`. Different `gh` subcommands using `--hostname` collapse into one `gh` family.
  WHY: A permission prompt for `gh --hostname ghe.example.com issue view 5` (a different subcommand) would be filed as a comment on the `gh` family issue instead of getting its own `gh issue` family issue, contrary to AD-1's goal of keeping subcommands apart. The `--hostname` flag is documented in `gh --help` and used in GitHub Enterprise environments.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
